clauses.text: 110 TWENTY-FOURTH REPORT OF CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. within the grade of classified laborer and at the same time prevent the promo- tion to a grade above that of classified laborer without examination. ASSISTANCE TO POBTO BICAN CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION. September 27, 1907. The United States Civil Service Commission is directed to render such assist- ance as may be practicable to the Porto Rican civil service commission, created under the insular legislative act of March 14, 1907, and officers and employees in the Federal service in Porto Rico shall facilitate the holding of examinations and other work of the Porto Rican civil service commission and render such other assistance as may be practicable. The United States Civil Service Com- mission may, in its discretion, authorize the transfer of employees from the civil service of Porto Rico to that of the United States, subject to the limitations respecting transfer within the Federal civil service. This order is similar to that signed by President McKinley on November 20, 11)00, in regard to the Philippine service. WAIVES OF EXAMINATION IN PROMOTION OB TRANSFER, November 22, 1907. When transfers or promotions are properly applied for and are otherwise per- missible, the Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized, in its discretion, looking to the good of the public service only, to waive requirements for exam- ination and to substitute for such examination so waived such other tests of fitness and capacity as the Commission may decide. In each case where such waiver is made the reasons therefor shall be stated at length by the Commission and made matter of record in its minutes. This order was recommended by the Commission for the reason that it was believed that the service would be benefited if the discretion of waiving ex- aminations in certain cases of transfer or promotion, where such examinations would ordinarily be required by the rules, should be placed in the hands of the Commission. CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION TO AID IN EXAMINATIONS FOR DESIGNATION FOB APPOINTMENT TO THE UNITED STATES MILITARY AND NAVAL ACADEMIES. December 17, 1907. Upon the request of any Member of Congress the United States Civil Service Commission shall aid in testing the qualifications of applicants for designation for api>ointnient in the United States Military or Naval academies, so far as this may be done without thereby adding to the expenses of the Commission. As the Commission has nli the facilities for holding such examinations, prac- tically without additional exj>ense, it was deemed advisable to secure authority from the President for holding such examinations. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR LEGISLATION. February 20, 1908. Hereafter the following procedure shall be strictly observed by officers and employees in the Executive civil service in submitting any recommendations affecting the method of api>oiutineut to any jiositioii or class of iN>sltions now included or which may Ik> included in the classified service under the operation of the civil-service act or rules: Every recommendation shall l>e accompanied by a full statement of the rea- sons therefor, and, if approved by the head of the pro]ter I Apartment or inde- jiendent bureau, shall be referred to the Civil Service Commission, which body shall submit a report thereon to the President. No recommendation of the diameter mentioned shall be submitted by any officer or employee, directly or indirectly, to Congress or to any committee or Member of Congress, except in the manner herein provided, unless such recom- mendation shall be called for from such officer or employee by the Senate, the House of liejtretieutatives, or the Congress.

648950Executive Order 1266 — Authorizing Civil Service Commission to Except Certain Unusual Positions from Examination1910President of the United States

The Civil Service Commission is hereby authorized to except from competitive examination, as contemplated by the civil-service act, section 2, clause Second, subject to the limitations prescribed by the statute and those now set forth in Rule II, certain positions arising, of unusual character, as to duties, and for which qualified persons are so rare that, in the judgment of the commission, they can not, in the interests of good civil-service administration, be filled through open competitive examination. In every instance of the exercise of this power the same procedure shall be followed as required in the Executive order of November 22, 1907.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

December 1, 1910.
